uvh26.title: The Urban Vision Hackathon Dataset and Models: Towards Image Annotations and Accurate Vision Models for Indian Traffic

clip.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
clip.training_data: WIT (WebImageText), 400M image-text pairs collected from the internet

contamination.conclusion: UVH-26 frames were captured in February 2025, four years after CLIP's training data was collected (model dated January 2021), so no test frame can be in CLIP's training set.
contamination.caveat: The concepts (auto-rickshaws, Indian buses, CCTV-style images) were certainly in CLIP's web data, so this tests transfer to a new camera domain, not unseen classes.
contamination.own_leakage: Prompts and the review threshold are chosen on val cameras only. Test pseudo-cameras share no group with val, but a by-eye audit (40 random test images vs their most similar val image, A1's protocol) found 4 same-camera pairs: val-test camera overlap is about 10% (95% CI about 4-23%); see test_val_leakage. Prompts are written from class definitions first and revised at most twice on val, so the effect of this overlap on the test numbers should be small. A1's test-vs-train figure (17.5%, CI 8.7-32%) does not apply here because nothing is trained.
contamination.a1_clip_use: Assignment 1 used CLIP ViT-B/32 embeddings only to compare grouping rules; the frozen split used 64x36 gradient-magnitude correlation, so no CLIP signal shaped the test set.

test_val_leakage.method: 40 random test images (numpy default_rng(seed=42).permutation), each paired with its most similar val image by 64x36 gradient-magnitude correlation g (A1 protocol); judged by eye: same / unclear / different
test_val_leakage.by: Claude judged all 40 pairs by eye at Yash's request; Yash spot-checked the 4 same-camera pairs
test_val_leakage.finding: Pairs #12 and #13 are the same camera at g ~ 0.25 because a large vehicle fills the frame and hides the static scene edges. So the g-based count (18 test images with a val neighbour at g >= 0.36, none at >= 0.48) is not an upper bound on overlap; the by-eye audit is the leakage estimate reported.
